$schema_note: Minimum-privilege IAM policy for the DAILY CORE-FACILITY USAGE INFERENCE Fargate task role (`python -m pipeline_cores.run --core 14 --with-affinity --alias-search --llm-carry-forward --with-method-families`). Attach to the role referenced by `cores_task_definition.json.taskRoleArn` (`reciterai-cores-task`). Modeled on `grants_task_iam_policy.json` minus its S3 WRITE statement: DynamoDB on the shared `reciterai` table, CloudWatch Logs on `/ecs/reciterai-cores`, and a read-only grant on the tools artifact prefix, nothing else. WHAT IS INCLUDED. (1) The DynamoDB statement's Action and Resource arrays are identical to enrichment/cold/grants; only the `Sid` is per-family, which is itself the convention in all four. Three call shapes are actually exercised and they are the whole surface: `UpdateItem` (persist.put_core_usage — one per surfaced (publication, core) row, SET what this run produced plus REMOVE the run.py-owned attributes it did not, per #384; and persist.put_core_staff_dict_counts — one per core in the DICTIONARY per run (fourteen, `--core` or not, since the counts describe the dictionary rather than the scoring pass), on PK=CORE#{core_id} / SK=STAFF_DICT, a targeted SET of `staff_count` and `staff_tracked_count` that names no other attribute and no other item. That write needs NO permission change: it is the same `dynamodb:UpdateItem` on the same `table/reciterai` already granted below, in a different partition, and the sibling CORE#{core_id}/CLIENTS item is reached by the GetItem below and never by this), `Scan` (persist.scan_prior_core_usage for the cross-run affinity prior under `--with-affinity`, and the carry-forward read of stored LLM evidence under `--llm-carry-forward` — both full-table paginated Scans with a server-side FilterExpression), and `GetItem` (persist.get_curated_clients on PK=CORE#14 / SK=CLIENTS, the list SPS's 'Known clients' panel writes). The true minimum is therefore GetItem + UpdateItem + Scan, and `.../index/*` is unused — nothing in pipeline_cores queries a GSI. Keeping the block identical to its three siblings is the deliberate choice: these four policies get diffed against each other whenever a table permission changes, and a uniquely-trimmed fourth copy reads as drift and gets 'fixed' back to the family shape. Trim it only if the cores task is ever moved off the shared table. (2) CloudWatch Logs is `CreateLogStream` + `PutLogEvents` scoped to `/ecs/reciterai-cores`. `logs:CreateLogGroup` is absent here AND on `ecsTaskExecutionRole`, which is exactly why the task definition omits `awslogs-create-group` and the log group is pre-created by hand (README step 1). (3) S3 READ on the tools artifact, and nothing else. `method_families.load_family_index` reads `tools/latest/tools.json` + `tools/latest/tool_context.json` from `wcmc-reciterai-artifacts` on every run carrying `--with-method-families`, so `s3:GetObject` on `wcmc-reciterai-artifacts/tools/*` is REQUIRED. pipeline_cores still publishes no artifact — its output is the DynamoDB rows SPS's nightly projects into MySQL — so this is read-only and there is no `{version}/`, no `latest/` pointer to write, and no shrink guard. THIS STATEMENT WAS MISSING WHEN THE FLAG SHIPPED, and the failure is worth recording because it is the opposite of quiet: `load_family_index` RAISES on a failed read rather than degrading to `{}` (an empty index would make `put_core_usage` REMOVE `method_tier`/`method_evidence` from every previously scored row), so the 2026-09-07 05:00 run died 3ms in on `AccessDenied` and core 14 got NO scoring pass at all — not merely no method signal. That is the guard working as designed; the grant was simply never added when `reciterai-cores:4` gained the flag. Anything that adds a NEW artifact read to this task needs a matching Resource here, and a local pre-flight run under an operator's own credentials CANNOT catch its absence — only the task role can. The OTHER S3 surface stays opt-in and out of the nightly command: `fulltext.PmcFullTextClient.with_s3()` (reached only via `--fulltext-s3`, warmed out of band by `python -m pipeline_cores.prefetch_fulltext`) reads and writes the shared PMC cache at `s3://wcmc-reciterai-artifacts/cores/fulltext/{pmid}.xml`. It is NOT running today and is NOT silently degrading — it is never constructed, because the flag is absent. Note its failure mode before adding that flag: the cache is best-effort by design and an AccessDenied degrades to an origin fetch with a single logged warning rather than raising, so adding `--fulltext-s3` WITHOUT also adding `s3:GetObject`+`s3:PutObject` on `wcmc-reciterai-artifacts/cores/fulltext/*` and `s3:ListBucket` on the bucket buys nothing and fails SILENTLY — the run just re-fetches from NCBI at full price. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY OMITTED. (4) NO SecretsManager statement. The four DB_* keys and `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` are injected as env vars by the EXECUTION role at container start, and nothing in the runtime path calls `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` — `utils.db.get_engine` reads DB_HOST/DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD/DB_NAME from the environment and `utils.dynamodb_helpers.get_dynamo_client` takes only a region. This follows the grants policy, NOT the cold one: cold's Secrets statement covers code paths pipeline_cores does not have. (5) NO `bedrock:InvokeModel`. Doubly absent: every `bedrock-runtime` call in this repo authenticates via the `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` bearer token rather than SigV4 against the task role (identical posture to enrichment/cold/grants/spotlight, and dropping the IAM grant gives loud-failure mode on a missing or stale token), and the nightly command makes no Bedrock call at all — `--with-llm` is deliberately not in it. An operator override to `--with-llm` therefore needs NO change to this policy. (6) NO outbound-network IAM of any kind is needed for the NCBI traffic `--alias-search` generates (eutils esearch + idconv + efetch over plain HTTPS) — that is a security-group concern, not a policy one; see eventbridge.json deploy_notes.ecs_targets.
